subject: 16 Foster Court Historic District
overview: The City Council received operational updates on Lawrence Memorial Hospital and local COVID-19 management, rejected a proposed historic district designation for 16 Foster Court, and referred a revised snow and ice removal ordinance to subcommittee.

items.title: Commendation for Stanley Chiozzi
items.summary: Approved a resolution congratulating Stanley Chiozzi on his 101st birthday.

items.title: Cannabis Advisory Committee Ordinance
items.summary: Tabled the draft ordinance to the next regular meeting to allow the city solicitor time to draft language.

items.title: Lawrence Memorial Hospital Campus Update
items.summary: Voted to reconvene in six months and adopted amendments requesting alternative design renderings for mechanical screening, parking lot fencing at 216 Governors Avenue, and traffic safety coordination.

items.title: Monthly COVID-19 Update
items.summary: Received a public health briefing from the Board of Health Director, and approved motions to broadcast flu clinic dates via robocall and request an emergency ordinance granting paid administrative leave for city employees quarantined due to occupational exposure.

items.title: Historic District Designation for 16 Foster Court
items.summary: Failed to approve the establishment of a single-parcel historic district at 16 Foster Court after a 3-4 roll call vote did not meet the required five-vote threshold.

items.title: Unsettled Municipal Union Contracts
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a list of unsettled collective bargaining agreements and associated external legal expenses.

items.title: Street and Driveway Repaving Requests
items.summary: Approved requests to repave Winslow Avenue between numbers 69 and 77 and repair the driveway apron at 9 Canal Street.

items.title: Snow and Ice Removal Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance shifting snow removal responsibilities to property owners to the Public Works Subcommittee, with amendments addressing accessibility clearances, senior and disabled assistance, and municipal clearing of priority corridors.

items.title: Common Victualler Licenses for BJ's Donuts
items.summary: Approved transfer of common victualler licenses for locations at 430 Salem Street and 620 Fellsway subject to 30- and 60-day reviews, while the petition for 278 Middlesex Avenue was withdrawn.

items.title: Medical Input on In-Person City Hall Meetings
items.summary: Approved a request for the Board of Health to seek opinions from partner physicians regarding criteria for resuming in-person meetings.

items.title: Legal Opinion on Chamber Capacity and Open Meeting Law
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a legal opinion from the city solicitor regarding potential Open Meeting Law conflicts related to room capacity limits.

items.title: Main Street and South Street Traffic Safety
items.summary: Referred the intersection safety review to the Transportation Subcommittee and requested temporary raised crosswalks and ongoing coordination with MassDOT and the state legislative delegation.

items.title: Employee Data Breach Inquiry
items.summary: Referred an inquiry regarding municipal and school employee personal data disclosure and remediation efforts to an executive session with the administration.

items.title: Mystic Valley Parkway Traffic Calming
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the Department of Conservation and Recreation and state legislators implement traffic calming and pedestrian crossings at the Mystic Valley Parkway and High Street.

items.title: Condolences and Memorials
items.summary: Observed moments of silence and dedicated proceedings in memory of longtime residents Joanne Caputo and Louise Musto-Choate.

items.title: Breast Cancer Awareness Month
items.summary: Approved a resolution acknowledging October as Breast Cancer Awareness Month and endorsing lighting the City Hall dome pink.

items.title: Household Hazardous Waste Disposal
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the administration examine establishing a local hazardous waste site and joining the Lexington regional disposal consortium.

items.title: Building Permit Historical Review Notifications
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the Building Department to notify permit applicants within 72 hours of receiving a determination from the Historical Commission.

items.title: Reports of Committees
items.summary: Received and approved committee reports covering the 16 Foster Court site visit, chamber reopening guidelines, zoning recodification, and municipal anti-racism initiatives.

items.title: Utility Pole Safety on Mangles Street
items.summary: Approved a resolution instructing the city wires inspector to demand immediate corrective action from National Grid regarding a leaning utility pole on Mangles Street.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the City Council meeting minutes of September 8, 2020, and September 22, 2020 as amended.
